name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
description: The monarch’s official residence in Scotland, at the foot of the Royal Mile, with Mary Queen of Scots’ rooms and a ruined abbey.

name: Edinburgh Castle
description: The fortress on a volcanic rock above the city, with the Scottish crown jewels, and the esplanade in front where the Tattoo is held.

name: National Museum of Scotland
description: A big museum of Scottish history, science and world cultures, with a rooftop terrace and Dolly the sheep.

name: Writers’ Museum
description: A 17th-century house off the Royal Mile with displays on Robert Burns, Walter Scott and Robert Louis Stevenson.

name: St Giles’ Cathedral
places: Heart of Midlothian mosaic (site of the Old Tolbooth)
description: Edinburgh’s main church, on the Royal Mile. In the cobbles outside, a heart marks the site of the old town prison.

name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
description: An old churchyard full of carved tombstones, with the statue of Greyfriars Bobby, the loyal terrier, by its gate.

name: Princes Street Gardens
description: A park in the valley below the castle, home to the Gothic spire of the Scott Monument, which you can climb.

name: Surgeons’ Hall Museums
description: Medical museums run by the Royal College of Surgeons, with anatomy and pathology collections and the history of surgery in the city.

name: Scottish Parliament
description: Scotland’s parliament building, opened in 2004, opposite Holyroodhouse. Visitors can tour it and watch debates.

name: Scottish National Gallery
description: Scotland’s national collection of fine art, from the Renaissance to the early 20th century, on the Mound above Princes Street Gardens.

name: Old College
places: Site of Kirk o’ Field, Old College
description: The university’s neoclassical quadrangle, built on the site of Kirk o’ Field, where Mary Queen of Scots’ husband was killed in 1567.
